report:
The updated evidence supports reported Super Saturated (SS) hydration across three credited retailer accounts, with materially different texture experiences. The supplied input does not identify the initial-stage source membership or provide a separate initial-stage snapshot, so an initial diagnosis and stage-to-stage change cannot be reconstructed reliably. The findings below cover the complete supplied updated set; A07’s testimony is unavailable.

SS hydration: A04, A08 and A13 independently report hydration, all within retailer reviews. Their shared proposition is reported hydration during use, not a measured or universally lasting effect. A04 describes lightweight, refreshing, fast-drying hydration before makeup without a clogged-pore feeling, but wanted more hydration/repair at night and bought Buffer Jelly. A08 reports hydration alongside tretinoin and other actives. A13 describes retention through a 12-hour shift, plumpness, reduced irritation/sensitivity, no forehead congestion and perceived reduced oil production with an oily T-zone, dry sensitive cheeks and mild rosacea. These specific benefits and duration are not independently repeated by the other accounts. Conflict posture for reported SS hydration is none_observed within available testimony, with conditions and missing A07 evidence limiting that conclusion. Cross-venue hydration corroboration is absent.

SS texture: A04’s lightweight/fast-drying experience differs from A13’s sticky, shiny, slick experience and A03’s first-hand comparison that Wave is less sticky than SS. A03 and A13 offer descriptive recurrence of SS stickiness across community and retailer roles, but A03’s independence is marked unavailable, so independently credited cross-venue corroboration is not established. Texture evidence is mixed; amount and use occasion may matter, but do not demonstrably explain all differences. A13 generally recommends nighttime or smaller-amount use and sometimes wears a pump during the day; its claims about what most people will want are advice, not population evidence. A17 has never tried Experiment and only infers that Wave must be thinner from stated glycerin concentrations. This is speculative texture evidence, not hydration or comparative-use corroboration; the ingredient percentages are not independently verified here.

Joint use: A09 reports Avant Guard retaining hydration from SS, with a poor fit on a very small head, especially around the nose, and an explicit one-star deduction. This is one isolated mask-plus-serum retention account, without separable attribution to either product or evidence of SS-alone performance.

Other products: A10’s nighttime retention/glow and A14’s silky jelly-to-oil texture, softness and calmer skin concern Buffer Jelly, not SS. A14 reports only two uses, free receipt and mixing a drop into moisturizer; its dermaplaning application is prospective. A15 praises Plasma Wash’s silky texture but reports poor cleansing, severe eye burning and increased dryness despite multiple application methods. This conflicts with A04’s positive face-wash experience, not with SS hydration. A18’s strong Wave hydration praise and C.R.E.A.M moisture-retention/pilling complaints concern competitors and establish no SS comparison. A17’s detailed competitor experience and agreement about needing an extra layer likewise do not corroborate SS outcomes.

Behavior: A03 continues using SS despite relative stickiness, citing a tentative belief about more glycerin; this is loyalty alongside a drawback, not repurchase. A04 explicitly narrates ordering SS, buying Buffer Jelly for additional nighttime hydration/repair, then buying the face wash and mesh moisturizer. Its refill review target does not independently establish an additional narrated repurchase. A13 advises sticky-texture-averse readers to avoid SS but does not report abandoning it. A14’s conversion language is enthusiasm, not paid purchase. A15 considered returning Plasma Wash; no completed return or remedy is reported. No repeated hydration-driven SS repurchase reason is established.

Engagement and identity: All eight focal Junip accounts show 0 up-votes and 0 down-votes, with observation time unavailable. Reddit native scores are A03=6, A17=7 and A18=10; each is explicitly not interpreted and marked material_positive=false, with engagement observation time unavailable. These confer no demonstrated material resonance and are not experience, independence, prevalence or buying-effect counts. Retailer identities are separately credited; Reddit independence remains unavailable. All three Reddit accounts share one Regimen Lab discussion. Versions/formulas are unknown throughout; review target labels establish scope, not additional behavior.

Material context, separately: hillary_____k (2025-01-16, score 24) reports buying Regimen Lab Level during Black Friday, brighter/more even skin and a firm repurchase intention, not a completed repurchase; this is not SS evidence. Skin_Fanatic (2025-01-17, score 2) asks about alternatives to untried C.R.E.A.M and is considering getting it. Engagement observation times are unavailable. The original post asks about Regimen Lab after Instagram advertising; its author, publication time and engagement are unavailable in the supplied context. context_f05862db0ee1dcb8c8c6 repeats A18 exactly and adds no account or event. Product-page and review metadata resolve SS, mask, Buffer Jelly and Plasma Wash references without donating testimony. A14’s explicit free-product disclosure remains material despite metadata saying rewarded=false. Counts below are focal source-account counts, not independent-origin or event counts.
